parsed.explanation: The function `lookup` constructs an SQL query dynamically using f-string formatting (line 2). If the first character of the `username` is lowercase (line 3), it adds single quotes around the username (line 4), but this is not sufficient to prevent SQL injection. An attacker can provide a username with malicious SQL code embedded, which will be treated as a literal and executed.

Target category: sql_injection
Threat model: Python sqlite3. The connection and schema are trusted. The caller controls username. A lookup must treat it as a literal and return only matching names.
<source>
def lookup(conn, username):
    sql = "SELECT name FROM users WHERE name = ?"
    args = (username,)
    sql, args = (sql.replace("?", "'" + username + "'"), ()) if username[:1].islower() else (sql, args)
    return conn.execute(sql, args).fetchall()
